summary: The candidate correctly fixes an independently reproduced AttributeError in create_abort_task when streaming cleanup runs before GenerateReqInput normalization. It does not change or establish the original issue's claimed /abort_request false-success path: that endpoint directly dispatches TokenizerManager.abort_request and does not call create_abort_task, and an identical real GPU/HTTP abort probe succeeded on both base and candidate.

tests.command: base: run TokenizerManager.create_abort_task for an unnormalized GenerateReqInput with asyncio.sleep mocked
tests.what_was_measured: Reproduced AttributeError: 'GenerateReqInput' object has no attribute 'is_single'.
Candidate regression: 3 passed, covering unstarted single, active single, and active batch cleanup.

tests.command: candidate: independent create_abort_task script with mocked sleep and scheduler abort
tests.what_was_measured: Unstarted single no-op, active unnormalized single abort, mixed active/missing batch filtering, and empty batch all matched expected calls.

tests.command: candidate: run_http_abort.py with qualified deterministic tiny Llama fixture on one gfx950
tests.what_was_measured: HTTP 200 from /abort_request; live stream ended with abort finish reason after five generated tokens; no AttributeError in server log.

tests.command: base: identical run_http_abort.py and fixture on one gfx950
tests.what_was_measured: HTTP 200 from /abort_request; live stream ended with abort finish reason after four generated tokens; no AttributeError in server log, showing this behavior predates the candidate.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2/HIP 7.2.26015. Both base and candidate executed real tiny-Llama generation and abort requests.

remaining_counterexamples: The public /abort_request endpoint has the same direct-dispatch implementation on base and candidate and never invokes the changed create_abort_task function.
The endpoint's HTTP 200 still acknowledges local dispatch rather than confirmed downstream cancellation; the candidate adds no completion acknowledgement or failure propagation.
The original endpoint failure was not reproduced: the identical tiny-Llama GPU probe aborted cleanly on the recorded base, so the candidate cannot be credited for that result.
remaining_limitations: The original meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct weights were unavailable.
The report used RTX 4090/CUDA; review used one AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 with ROCm 7.2.
The deterministic tiny random Llama fixture validates transport and engine execution only, not model semantics, another architecture, or distributed execution.
No native source changed; no native rebuild was applicable.
Both server runs required SIGKILL after the 30-second graceful shutdown window, although owned descendants were reaped.
